title: The animal kingdom: invertebrates and vertebrates
summary: How do you tell the invertebrate phyla and vertebrate classes apart?
cards.0.p: Animals are eukaryotic, multicellular and heterotrophic. In other words, they take in ready-made food by swallowing it. Their cells have no cell wall. Most of them move, and their muscle and nerve tissues let them react quickly.
cards.0.svg#8: Adult sponges and corals stay attached to one spot
cards.0.key: Animal cells have no wall. Plants have a cellulose wall, and fungi have a chitin wall.
cards.0.once.soru: An organism is multicellular, has no cell wall and takes in food by swallowing it. Which kingdom is it in?
cards.0.once.secenekler.0.neden: Animals are multicellular, have no cell wall and are heterotrophs. They take in food by swallowing it.
cards.0.once.secenekler.1.neden: Plants have a cellulose wall, and they carry out photosynthesis.
cards.0.once.secenekler.2.neden: Fungi have a chitin wall. They digest food outside the body and absorb it.
cards.1.p: Vertebrates have a backbone made of vertebrae along their back, and it protects the spinal cord. Invertebrates have no backbone, but some of them have an exoskeleton. About 95% of animal species are invertebrates.
cards.1.key: Not every animal with a skeleton is a vertebrate. For example, an insect has an exoskeleton but no backbone.
cards.1.etk.soru: Put each animal in the right group.
cards.1.etk.ogeler.0.2: It has an internal skeleton of chalky plates under its skin, but no backbone.
cards.1.etk.ogeler.1.2: It has well-developed eyes and a nervous system, but it is a mollusk and has no backbone.
cards.1.etk.ogeler.5.2: Its skeleton is made of cartilage, but it has a backbone. It is a cartilaginous fish.
cards.1.etk.ogeler.7.2: It looks like a fish, but it is a mammal and a vertebrate.
cards.2.p: Sponges have no true tissues. They feed by filtering food out of the water that flows through the pores in their body. Cnidarians such as jellyfish, corals and hydras have two cell layers and hunt with the stinging cells on their tentacles.
cards.2.key: Sponges have no tissues, and their body is full of pores. Cnidarians have two layers. They have tentacles and stinging cells.
cards.2.once.soru: A sponge passes water through the holes in its body. How does it get its food?
cards.2.once.secenekler.0.neden: A sponge filters the food carried by the water that enters its pores. An adult sponge lives attached to one spot.
cards.2.once.secenekler.1.neden: A sponge has no tentacles and no mouth.
cards.2.once.secenekler.2.neden: Animals do not carry out photosynthesis.
cards.3.p: Flatworms have a flattened body, and most are parasites. Roundworms have a separate mouth and anus. The body of segmented worms is made of rings. They have a closed circulatory system, which means the blood always stays inside vessels.
cards.3.key: A tapeworm has no digestive system. It absorbs digested food through its body surface.
cards.3.once.soru: A tapeworm lives in the human intestine and has no digestive system. How does it feed?
cards.3.once.secenekler.0.neden: A tapeworm absorbs the digested food in the intestine through its body surface. It is a parasitic flatworm.
cards.3.once.secenekler.1.neden: A tapeworm does not suck blood. It absorbs the ready food in the intestine.
cards.3.once.secenekler.2.neden: Animals do not carry out photosynthesis.
cards.4.p: Mollusks have a soft body. Most of them have a chalky shell made by the mantle. A snail's shell is one piece, while a mussel's shell has two parts. An octopus has no outer shell, and it is a very intelligent animal.
cards.4.svg#9: Shared: soft body, mantle, muscular foot
cards.4.key: Most mollusks have open circulation, but the octopus has closed circulation.
cards.4.once.soru: Which one has no outer shell but is still a mollusk?
cards.4.once.secenekler.0.neden: An octopus has no outer shell. It is an intelligent mollusk with well-developed eyes and a nervous system.
cards.4.once.secenekler.1.neden: A snail has a one-piece shell.
cards.4.once.secenekler.2.neden: A mussel has a two-part shell.
cards.5.p: The largest phylum is the arthropods. Their body is covered by an exoskeleton made of chitin, and they molt in order to grow. An insect has 3 pairs of legs, and a spider has 4 pairs. That is why a spider is not an insect.
cards.5.svg#22: They molt in order to grow
cards.5.key: An insect's body has 3 parts, and it has 3 pairs of legs and antennae. A spider's body has 2 parts, and it has 4 pairs of legs and no antennae.
cards.6.p: Echinoderms such as starfish and sea urchins live only in the sea. They have an internal skeleton made of chalky plates. The adults have radial symmetry and move with their tube feet.
cards.6.key: Echinoderms have an internal skeleton, but no backbone. That is why they are invertebrates.
cards.6.once.soru: A starfish has an internal skeleton of chalky plates under its skin. Is a starfish a vertebrate?
cards.6.once.secenekler.0.neden: A starfish has an internal skeleton, but no backbone. That is why it is an invertebrate.
cards.6.once.secenekler.1.neden: Having an internal skeleton does not mean having a backbone.
cards.6.once.secenekler.2.neden: A starfish larva has no backbone either.
cards.7.p: Fish breathe with gills and swim with fins. Their heart has two chambers, and their body temperature changes with the surroundings. A shark's skeleton is made of cartilage, while an anchovy's skeleton is made of bone.
cards.7.svg#14: Only oxygen-poor blood passes through the heart
cards.7.key: Only oxygen-poor blood passes through a fish's heart. The blood picks up oxygen in the gills.
cards.7.once.soru: How does a fish breathe in water?
cards.7.once.secenekler.0.neden: Gills take up the oxygen dissolved in the water.
cards.7.once.secenekler.1.neden: Most fish have no lungs. Fish breathe with gills.
cards.7.once.secenekler.2.neden: Breathing through the skin matters for frogs. A fish breathes with gills.
cards.8.p: Amphibians such as frogs and salamanders lay eggs without shells in water. Their larvae are called tadpoles, and a tadpole breathes with gills. The tadpole goes through metamorphosis and turns into an adult with lungs. An amphibian's heart has three chambers.
cards.8.svg#12: Blood partly mixes in the ventricle
cards.8.svg#13: Skin is moist, bare and full of glands
cards.8.key: A frog's skin must stay moist, because breathing through the skin only works when the skin is moist.
cards.8.once.soru: A tadpole, the young of a frog, breathes with gills in water. What does an adult frog breathe with?
cards.8.once.secenekler.0.neden: The lungs develop during metamorphosis. An adult frog also breathes through its moist skin.
cards.8.once.secenekler.2.neden: An adult frog also has lungs. Breathing through the skin only helps them.
cards.9.p: Reptiles have dry, scaly skin. This reduces water loss. Reptiles breathe with lungs and lay shelled eggs on land. Most have a three-chambered heart, but a crocodile's heart has four chambers. Their body temperature changes with the surroundings.
cards.9.svg#12: Dry, scaly skin and shelled eggs
cards.9.key: A crocodile's heart has four chambers, but its body temperature still varies.
cards.10.p: Feathers are found only in birds. Birds have hollow, light bones. They also have air sacs. Their heart has four chambers, and their body temperature is constant. Birds lay shelled eggs.
cards.10.key: Air sacs make air flow in one direction through a bird's lungs.
cards.11.p: What sets mammals apart from other animals is hair and the mammary glands that feed the young with milk. The diaphragm helps with breathing. Their heart has four chambers, and their body temperature is constant. The platypus lays eggs, but it nurses its young.
cards.11.svg#0: All have: hair, mammary glands, diaphragm,
cards.11.svg#1: a four-chambered heart, constant body temperature
cards.11.svg#11: Whales and dolphins are placental mammals too
cards.11.key: A dolphin looks like a fish, but it breathes with lungs and nurses its young. That is why it is a mammal.
cards.12.p: In fish, amphibians and reptiles, body temperature changes along with the surroundings. These animals slow down in the cold. Birds and mammals, however, make heat through metabolism and keep it in with feathers, hair or a layer of fat. That is why their body temperature is constant.
cards.12.svg#33: Only birds and mammals keep a constant temperature
cards.12.key: A constant body temperature is found only in birds and mammals.
cards.13.p: A sponge has no nerve cells. A hydra has a net-like nervous system, a planarian has a ladder-like one, and an insect has one with a chain of ganglia. Vertebrates have a brain and a spinal cord.
cards.13.svg#8: simple to complex: nerve cells gather at the front
cards.13.key: The gathering of nerve cells in the head region is called cephalization.
cards.13.once.soru: A jellyfish has no brain, but when you touch it, its whole body reacts. What is its nervous system like?
cards.13.once.secenekler.0.neden: In hydras and jellyfish, nerve cells spread through the body like a net. That is why a signal travels in every direction.
cards.13.once.secenekler.1.neden: A brain and a spinal cord are found in vertebrates.
cards.13.once.secenekler.2.neden: The animals with no nerve cells are sponges. A jellyfish has nerve cells.
cards.14.p:
• Animals are eukaryotic, multicellular and heterotrophic. Their cells have no wall.
• About 95% of species are invertebrates. The largest phylum is the arthropods.
• The heart has 2 chambers in fish, 3 in amphibians and most reptiles, and 4 in birds and mammals.
• Body temperature is constant only in birds and mammals.
quiz.0.q: Match each animal with its phylum.
quiz.0.e: A jellyfish is a cnidarian with stinging cells, a tapeworm is a flatworm, and a leech is a segmented worm. An octopus is a mollusk without a shell, and a starfish is an echinoderm.
quiz.1.q: Sort each animal by its body temperature.
quiz.1.e: Body temperature is constant only in birds and mammals. A penguin is a bird. A bat, a dolphin and a platypus are mammals. In fish, amphibians and reptiles, body temperature varies.
quiz.2.q: Match each set of features with its vertebrate class.
quiz.2.ciftler.1.0: Moist skin and lungs, three chambers
quiz.2.e: Gills and a two-chambered heart belong to fish, and moist skin and a three-chambered heart belong to amphibians. Dry scaly skin and shelled eggs belong to reptiles. Feathers are found only in birds, and hair and mammary glands only in mammals.
quiz.3.q: Which feature shows for certain that an animal is a vertebrate?
quiz.3.o.1: A backbone made of vertebrae along its back
quiz.3.o.2: A skeleton that supports its body
quiz.3.e: Earthworms and octopuses also have closed circulation. Arthropods have a skeleton too, in the form of an exoskeleton. Fish breathe with gills, not lungs. The feature that defines a vertebrate is the backbone.
quiz.3.y.0: Invertebrates such as the earthworm also have closed circulation. What sets vertebrates apart is the backbone.
quiz.3.y.2: An insect's exoskeleton also supports its body. What shows for certain that an animal is a vertebrate is a backbone made of vertebrae.
quiz.3.y.3: Fish are vertebrates, but they breathe with gills. The sure test is having a backbone.
A:ozet: Try first, then learn the name. Find the backbone, count the legs, build the heart and compare body temperatures.
A:adimlar.0.metin: Look at the skeletons of three animals. Find which one has a backbone.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: An insect has a hard exoskeleton, but no backbone.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: A starfish has an internal skeleton of chalky plates under its skin, but no backbone. Echinoderms are invertebrates.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: A fish has a backbone made of vertebrae along its back. The spinal cord runs through this bony canal.
A:adimlar.1.metin: A spider has 8 legs, and an insect has 6. There are 2 spiders in the garden. Add enough insects to make 34 legs in total.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.tamam: 2 spiders have 16 legs, and 3 insects have 18. That makes 34 legs in total.
A:adimlar.2.metin: In vertebrates, the number of heart chambers differs from group to group. Change the number of chambers and watch how the blood flows. Then build a bird's heart.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.tamam: In a four-chambered heart, oxygen-rich and oxygen-poor blood never mix. This is how the large amount of oxygen needed for flight is supplied.
A:adimlar.3.metin: Change the outside temperature and compare the two animals.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.soru: A mouse and a lizard are about the same size. Which one has to eat more food?
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: A lizard does not burn food to warm its body. It gets heat from the sun and its surroundings.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: A mouse makes the heat it needs to keep its body at 37 °C by burning food. The colder it gets, the more it has to eat.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Lower the outside temperature to 5 °C. The mouse is still at 37 °C. Think about where that heat comes from.
A:adimlar.4.metin: An animal breathes with lungs. Its heart has four chambers, but its body temperature is variable. Change the number of chambers and see how many chambers each group has.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: An eagle's heart has four chambers, but its body temperature is constant.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: A frog's heart has three chambers.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: A crocodile is a reptile, but its heart has four chambers. Even so, its body temperature varies. So a four-chambered heart alone does not mean a constant temperature.
A:adimlar.5.metin: A bat can fly. Look at its features one by one and find its class.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.soru: Which class is the bat in?
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: A bat has no feathers. Flying is not unique to birds.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: A bat has hair and feeds its young with milk, so it is a mammal. Its wing is skin stretched between its long fingers.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Reptiles have dry, scaly skin, and their body temperature varies. A bat has hair, and its body temperature is constant.
A:kapanis.0: Animals are eukaryotic, multicellular and heterotrophic. Their cells have no wall.
A:kapanis.1: What shows an animal is a vertebrate is not a skeleton but a backbone. About 95% of species are invertebrates, and the largest phylum is the arthropods.
A:kapanis.2: An insect has 3 pairs of legs, and a spider has 4 pairs. That is why a spider is not an insect.
A:kapanis.3: The heart has 2 chambers in fish, 3 in amphibians and most reptiles, and 4 in birds, mammals and crocodiles.
A:kapanis.4: Body temperature is constant only in birds and mammals. Feathers are unique to birds, and hair and mammary glands to mammals.
